Independent analytic reconstruction of Calkin spectrum, index/divisibility homotopy and exact minimizer
correctness.rationale: For a>b and k not dividing p, the unitary image of S in the Calkin algebra has full circle spectrum by rotation invariance; the two-scale direct sum is normal there. At every z on the midpoint circle its inverse resolvent norm is exactly 1/δ, δ=(a−b)/2. The index of aS−z is −1 inside radius a by the Fredholm path to aS, and bS−z is invertible outside radius b, so the sum has index −p. A strict essential-norm perturbation below δ preserves that index by the Neumann homotopy. If the perturbation is to X^k, spectral mapping implies X−w is Fredholm on the connected circle |w|=((a+b)/2)^(1/k), so its index is constant. The k commuting linear factors at each z add k copies of that index, contradicting k not dividing p. For the upper bound, S^k interleaves k copies of S. Interleaving the total at scale (a+b)/2 gives a power at norm δ, and the essential lower bound forces essential norm δ as well. If each multiplicity is divisible, the scales interleave separately; if a=b, interleave the divisible total. Swapping scales exchanges p and q, whose divisibility agrees. This establishes both infima and attainment with unrestricted bounded X.
residual_risks: The verified statement assumes positive constant scales and a finite total multiplicity divisible by k. It does not classify minimizers or general weighted shifts. No numerical or formal proof certification is claimed.

value.rationale: Sharp metric stability for a concrete family of shift powers, allowing unrestricted perturbations and showing the same obstruction modulo compacts, is a useful strengthening of root-existence and qualitative closure statements. It identifies exactly how much changing the scales must cost and supplies a realizable midpoint benchmark for all admissible multiplicities and root orders.
residual_risks: Value concerns the two-scale family and exact sharpness, not a general theorem for arbitrary weighting or all multiplicities.
